No Close Reason, Abandonment Reason, Close Review or Abandonment (D6)

No Terminal Disposition, because no effective disposing facts exist
No valuation, marked P&L, Overrun or Expiration Payoff curve
Only two of the seven fixed Journal Entry Types and two of the seven Sources exist (D17)
Unsaved form state surviving a resize is required behavior and not stored evidence
Stored Lifecycle State and derived expected Lifecycle State are shown as separate concepts
No statement about startup or open-list timing
Native <select> controls set by value rather than synthetic arrow keys in automated runs

entries.expected: A Plan whose conditions yield no positive monetary risk is rejected with a typed message naming the offending condition, and nothing is saved (no Trade, no Journal Entry, unchanged revisions).
entries.actual: The Plan was saved with 1R "500" although both declared monetary boundaries were 0; counts {"journal":2,"lifecycleIndex":0,"lifecycleListProjection":0,"marketData":0,"referenceCatalog":3,"tradeLifecycle":0,"tradeRecord":0,"tradeVersion":0,"workspaceMeta":2} → {"journal":3,"lifecycleIndex":1,"lifecycleListProjection":0,"marketData":0,"referenceCatalog":3,"tradeLifecycle":1,"tradeRecord":5,"tradeVersion":1,"workspaceMeta":2}. The only UI path to a numeric-baseline rejection is a wrong-side Stop (flow 6) or non-numeric text, whose message does not name a condition. Stored Plan row: perConditionBasis monetaryBoundary 0 USD for both conditions with policy NearestNonnegativeMonetaryBoundary, while originalPlannedRisk/oneR are 500 USD. The form also offers no way to remove a Stop or change a condition's role (condition 1 is always Stop, condition 2 always Target, added conditions default to Stop), so the only price-based route to a non-positive risk is flow 6's wrong-side Stop.
